title: Global-section unit and inverse associativity equations for scheme module adjoints
statement: Let schemes lie in the fixed size convention [def-weil-size-convention, def-pc-scheme]. For every scheme morphism $a:A\to B$ choose a functor $L_a:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_A)$ on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and an adjunction $L_a\dashv a_*$. Let $c_{a,b}:L_aL_b\simeq L_{ba}$ be the normalized left-adjoint composition isomorphism induced by the canonical composition comparison for scheme module pushforwards, and let $i_A:L_{\mathrm{id}_A}\simeq\mathrm{id}$ be induced by the identity pushforward comparison. Write $u_a(F):\Gamma(B,F)\to\Gamma(A,L_aF)$ for the adjunction unit on the top open, followed by restriction from its inverse image to the top open. Then three formulas hold. For $b:A\to B$ and any module $F$ on $B$, $\Gamma(\mathrm{eq}_{\mathrm{id}\,b=b})\Gamma(c_{\mathrm{id}_A,b,F})u_{\mathrm{id}_A}(L_bF)=\mathrm{id}$. For $s\in\Gamma(A,L_{b\,\mathrm{id}_B}F)$, $\Gamma(L_b i_B)(\Gamma(c_{b,\mathrm{id}_B,F}^{-1})(s))=s$. Finally, for $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to C$, $d:C\to D$ and $F$ on $D$, $c_{ab,d,F}^{-1}$ followed by $c_{a,b,L_dF}^{-1}$ followed by $L_a(c_{b,d,F})$ equals $c_{a,bd,F}^{-1}$. Equality transports are those from the identity and associativity laws of scheme composition. These are the specific comparisons returned by Mathlib's leftAdjointCompIso and leftAdjointIdIso, not arbitrary isomorphisms.

proof.text: Scheme module pushforward identity and composition comparisons satisfy both unitality and associativity equations on every section, by reflexivity. Apply Mathlib leftAdjointCompIso_comp_id and leftAdjointCompIso_id_comp to transfer these two unit equations to left adjoints. The conjugate unit equation cancels the normalized identity comparison on global sections, proving the first formula. Cancelling the inverse composition comparison gives the second.

Apply leftAdjointCompIso_assoc to the canonical pushforward composition comparisons. Evaluate its component at F. Multiply by the inverses of the first two composition comparisons; categorical associativity and inverse cancellation give the third formula. All inverse-image-top restrictions are identity maps. No tensor construction, quasi-coherence or local trivialization is used.

theorem section_adjunction_coordinate_coherence
    (L : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}}, (A ⟶ B) → B.Modules ⥤ A.Modules)
    (adj : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (f : A ⟶ B), L f ⊣ Modules.pushforward f) :
    let c : ∀ {A B C : Scheme.{u}} (a : A ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ C),
        L b ⋙ L a ≅ L (a ≫ b) :=
      fun {_ _ _} a b ↦ Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso (adj b) (adj a) (adj (a ≫ b))
        (Modules.pushforwardComp a b)
    let unit : ∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (a : A ⟶ B) (F : B.Modules),
        Γ(F, ⊤) ⟶ Γ((L a).obj F, ⊤) :=
      fun {_ _} a F ↦ ((adj a).unit.app F).app ⊤ ≫
        ((L a).obj F).presheaf.map (homOfLE a.preimage_top.ge).op
    (∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (b : A ⟶ B) (F : B.Modules),
      unit (𝟙 A) ((L b).obj F) ≫ ((c (𝟙 A) b).hom.app F).app ⊤ ≫
        (eqToHom (congrArg (fun f ↦ (L f).obj F) (Category.id_comp b))).app ⊤ = 𝟙 _) ∧
    (∀ {A B : Scheme.{u}} (b : A ⟶ B) (F : B.Modules)
      (s : Γ((L (b ≫ 𝟙 B)).obj F, ⊤)),
      ((L b).map ((Adjunction.leftAdjointIdIso (adj (𝟙 B))
        (Modules.pushforwardId B)).hom.app F)).app ⊤
          (((c b (𝟙 B)).inv.app F).app ⊤ s) = s) ∧
    (∀ {A B C D : Scheme.{u}} (a : A ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ C) (d : C ⟶ D) (F : D.Modules),
      (c (a ≫ b) d).inv.app F ≫ (c a b).inv.app ((L d).obj F) ≫
        (L a).map ((c b d).hom.app F) = (c a (b ≫ d)).inv.app F)
